Change the cart and discount. Run the same boundary check before and after a code change, then test the repair.

What this build does

Runs a browser port of the demo-store coupon fixture. It does not fetch GitHub pull requests, call Nemotron, execute Python, or use a GPU. The full application runs separately on the Dell; live Nebius inference is currently blocked by unavailable account credits.

The manually defined repair passes this boundary check. This is not an automatically generated or fully verified repository repair.

The check you just ran

expected = max(cart_total - coupon_discount, 0)
assert baseline_result == expected
assert changed_result == expected

Amounts are evaluated as integer cents. Passing one check is evidence within that scope; it does not prove the absence of other bugs.
